security_audit.summary: This community skill intentionally launches external coding-agent CLIs and includes helper code that executes caller-provided command strings across operating systems. Most documentation-only alerts are false positives, but command execution, insecure temp logging, approval bypass guidance, and context forwarding are real risks.

remediation.suggestion: Default cookbooks to sandboxed execution and explicit approvals. Remove dangerous bypass and force-allow modes from default command examples.
Avoid shell=True and string-built shell commands. Build allowlisted argv arrays for each supported CLI and quote all paths safely.
Use secure tempfile APIs, restrictive permissions, unpredictable names, and cleanup. Avoid logging prompts or full debug output by default.
Require explicit consent before forwarding conversation summaries. Redact secrets and identify the target provider before spawning the agent.

semantic_findings.title: Dangerous Auto-Approval Defaults
semantic_findings.description: The Codex cookbook says to always use a sandbox and approval bypass flag, and the Cursor cookbook recommends force-allow command execution. These defaults remove key safety controls for autonomous coding agents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited prose directly instructs use of dangerous approval bypass or force-allow modes. This is intent-level risk that static pattern matching did not fully capture.

semantic_findings.title: Conversation History Forwarding to Spawned Agents
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs the caller to place conversation history and the next request into a prompt passed to another agent. This can disclose sensitive project or user context to a separate CLI or provider.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instructions explicitly require copying conversation history into a prompt template for the forked agent. Disclosure depends on user content, but the data flow is clear.

content.user_title: Spawn AI Coding Agents in New Terminals
content.value_statement: Running several coding assistants from terminals can be repetitive and easy to misconfigure. This skill provides cookbook-guided launch patterns for common AI coding CLIs.
actual_capabilities: Selects Claude Code by default, or uses a requested agent when enabled.
Reads a provider cookbook before building the CLI command.
Launches local terminals on macOS, Windows, WSL, Linux, or tmux.
Captures clean agent output or debug output to a returned file path.
Provides authentication fallback flows for Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude.
limitations: Requires the selected CLI to be installed and authenticated locally.
Some cookbook examples use broad auto-approval or sandbox bypass flags.
Captured output can include sensitive prompts, responses, or debug data.
The terminal helper does not safely parse arbitrary command strings.

use_cases.title: Parallel Code Review
use_cases.description: Launch a second coding agent to inspect a refactor while the primary session continues.

use_cases.title: CLI Workflow Comparison
use_cases.description: Compare how Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, OpenCode, or Copilot handle the same task.

use_cases.title: Interactive Auth Handoff
use_cases.description: Open a dedicated terminal for provider login when an agent reports an authentication failure.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Agent Spawn
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn an agent to review the current changes and summarize the main risks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Provider
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Codex to inspect the failing tests and suggest the next debugging steps.

prompt_templates.title: Include Conversation Context
prompt_templates.scenario: Pass a summary to the new agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Gemini with a summary of this conversation, then ask it to find edge cases in the parser.

prompt_templates.title: Captured Review Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Spawn Cursor Agent with captured output enabled. Compare the migration plan with the implementation and return a concise risk report.

output_examples.input: Spawn Claude Code to review a refactor with captured output.
output_examples.output: A new terminal opens in the current workspace. The skill returns the captured output path for later review.

output_examples.input: Use Codex to compare two implementation approaches.
output_examples.output: The skill selects the Codex cookbook, checks available CLI options, and launches an interactive Codex terminal.

output_examples.input: Open an auth terminal after a Cursor login failure.
output_examples.output: A provider login command opens in a separate terminal. The caller can retry after authentication completes.

best_practices: Review the selected cookbook before running any generated command.
Prefer sandboxed execution and explicit approvals for untrusted repositories.
Delete captured output files when they may contain sensitive context.
anti_patterns: Do not pass secrets inside prompts that will be logged or shared.
Do not use dangerous approval bypass flags on untrusted codebases.
Do not treat captured debug output as safe for public sharing.

faq.question: Which agents can this skill launch?
faq.answer: It documents launch patterns for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot.

faq.question: Does it install the agent CLIs?
faq.answer: No. The selected CLI must already be installed and available in the local environment.

faq.question: Does it run local commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It launches terminal commands, so users should review each command before execution.

faq.question: Where is captured output stored?
faq.answer: The helper uses temporary output paths such as local tmp directories or the Windows TEMP directory.

faq.question: Can it pass conversation history to another agent?
faq.answer: Yes, when requested with a summary flow. Users should redact sensitive details first.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted repositories?
faq.answer: Use caution. Some cookbook defaults bypass approvals or sandboxing and should be changed first.
